title: A2DP audio input decision: evaluate CPU/complexity trade-off on Pi Zero W
Implement OTA Updater service (Rust + NixOS)
description: The OTA updater is the #1 implementation priority. It enables CI/CD on the device — push a new release, the speaker pulls and applies it automatically. This is the force multiplier that makes everything else fast. Dependencies: KDS-d5m (NixOS validation must pass first). Scope: GitHub Releases check, download closures, nixos-rebuild switch, auto-rollback on boot failure, scheduled reboot in low-activity window, API endpoints (/api/ota/*), WebSocket events, Web UI update section.

title: Set up GitHub Actions CI/CD: build NixOS image + release on tag
description: CI/CD pipeline that builds the NixOS SD image and publishes it as a GitHub Release. This closes the loop with the OTA updater — tag a release, CI builds, device pulls it. Without this, OTA has nothing to fetch. Scope: GitHub Actions workflow, Nix build for cross-compilation (ARMv6 from x86_64), SD image artifact, release creation with closure + SHA256 manifest. Dependencies: KDS-eeu (flake must exist first).

Validate NixOS on Raspberry Pi Zero W (ARMv6)
description:
NixOS ARMv6 validation plan (no code yet — design phase only):

STEP 1 — Build in CI (automated):
- Write a NixOS flake with minimal config (kernel + ALSA + systemd)
- GitHub Actions cross-compiles sd-image-raspberrypi for armv6l
- If the build fails → NixOS ARMv6 is not viable, move to Plan B (Pi OS + RAUC)
- If the build succeeds → publish SD image as CI artifact

STEP 2 — Boot test on real hardware:
- Flash CI artifact to SD card
- Boot Pi Zero W from it
- Verify: kernel loads, ALSA devices appear, systemd starts, ssh access
- Verify: snd-soc-iqaudio-codec loads, snd-aloop loads
- If boot fails → check if it's a config issue (fixable) or fundamental ARMv6 gap (not fixable)

STEP 3 — Full platform test:
- Deploy full NixOS config (all 8 services)
- Verify ALSA loopback, CamillaDSP, BlueZ, Piper all work on ARMv6
- Measure CPU and memory under load

If STEP 1 fails → immediately pivot to Raspberry Pi OS + RAUC (Plan B)
If STEP 1 passes but STEP 2 fails → diagnose, may still pivot
If STEP 2 passes → NixOS confirmed, proceed with KDS-eeu (full flake)

title: Set up NixOS flake for the entire software platform
description: Define the entire system in a NixOS flake: kernel + HAT driver overlay, ALSA loopback, CamillaDSP service, all platform services (API Server, Audio Player, BT, TTS, OTA), systemd units, persistent data partition. This is the foundation for the OTA updater — without a flake, there's nothing atomic to deploy. Dependencies: KDS-d5m (NixOS validation).

Investigate per-source ALSA loopback channel architecture
description:
RESOLVED: CamillaDSP supports everything we need.

CONFIRMED CAPABILITIES:
- 5 faders (Main + Aux1-4) with independent volume/mute via websocket
- Volume filters in pipeline assigned to any Aux fader
- Per-source volume control at runtime — no config reload
- Smooth ramping (400ms default) on all volume changes
- Bluetooth capture natively via BlueZ (v2.0+)
- Multi-channel capture from single ALSA device

ARCHITECTURE DECISION:
- Single snd-aloop device with 6 channels (3 stereo pairs)
- ch0-1: Main audio (Spotify/AirPlay/Radio) — one at a time
- ch2-3: TTS Engine — independent
- ch4-5: Bluetooth A2DP — independent
- CamillaDSP mixer routes each pair through Volume filter + fader
- TTS ducking: SetFaderVolume(Main, -20dB) → play → restore
- Source switching: Audio Player just swrites to ch0-1, no CamillaDSP changes

REMAINING TODO: Test on real hardware that 3+ sources can write to different
subdevices simultaneously without xruns on Pi Zero W.
